title: A funding target for every product.
lead: The flight controller and ESC are in their first production batch, paid for and shipping late October 2026. The receivers, frames and motors are funded here: every product option has a public target, the quantity we order from the supplier. Your preorder pays for that run, and you can watch each target fill.

s1_body: OpenDrone is an open source FPV platform. The flight controller, ESC and receiver are open hardware with public design files. The frame design files are not public yet. The motors come from a motor manufacturer; we select and test them, and they are not open hardware.
Preorders pay for the supplier orders. Where each design stands, from first prototype to production, is on [the roadmap](/roadmap).
s2_body: Suppliers do not produce single units. Each sets a minimum order quantity, the smallest run it will make, and that quantity is the target for the product option.

When a target is reached we place the supplier order, and the product ships about 10 weeks later. Every target has a deadline: 31 December 2026. If the target is reached by 31 December 2026, the product ships by 11 March 2027 at the latest. Orders keep coming in after a target is reached: they fill the next batch, which gets its own target.
s3_body: The stack is the flight controller and the ESC, mounted on top of each other in the middle of the frame. Batch 1, 250 of each board in each size, is paid for and in production. It ships late October 2026.
Once batch 1 is gone, the stack gets a funding target like every other product.
s4_body: You pay in full when you order. The price steps up per product option as paid orders come in: units 1 to 100 cost 20% less than the retail price, units 101 to 250 cost 10% less, and from unit 251 the retail price applies. The price shown when you order is the price you pay. The product page shows how many units are left at the current price and what the next unit costs.

Shipping is a flat rate per order, charged at checkout: €8.50 to Belgium, €9.95 to Germany, France, Luxembourg and the Netherlands, €12.95 to most other EU countries. Every rate is on [the shipping page](/shipping). We do not collect import duties at checkout: outside the EU, including the United States, the carrier collects any import duties and taxes from you on delivery.
s5_body: An order ships once, complete. If you order the stack together with a product that is still funding, the whole order waits until everything in it is ready, which can be as late as March 2027. Order separately if you want the stack in October.
s6_body: Hardware schedules slip. Supplier lead times move, a component goes out of stock and has to be replaced by an equivalent, and a production run can need rework. When a ship date moves, you get mail with the new date.

A product can also fall short of its target. If a target is not reached by 31 December 2026, we mail everyone who ordered that product and each buyer chooses: a refund of everything paid for that product within 14 days, or keep the order for the new ship date in that mail.
s7_body: Incutec BV, a small company in Leuven, Belgium. The same people design the boards, answer the support mail and pack the parcels.
This is not a crowdfunding platform: you order in our own shop, under [our terms](/algemene-voorwaarden), article 7bis.
faq_a1: In full when you order: the product price and shipping. We charge nothing after checkout. Outside the EU, including the United States, the carrier may collect import duties and taxes from you on delivery: see [Shipping](/shipping).
faq_a2: The stack ships late October 2026 while batch 1 lasts. Every other product ships about 10 weeks after its target is reached. Every target has a deadline of 31 December 2026: if the target is reached by then, the product ships by 11 March 2027 at the latest. Each item shows its ship date on the product page, at checkout and on the order confirmation.
faq_q3: What happens when a target is reached?
faq_a3: We place the supplier order and mail everyone who ordered that product. You hear from us again when the ship date is set and before dispatch.
faq_q9: What if a target is not reached?
faq_a9: Every target has a deadline: 31 December 2026. If a product misses it, we mail everyone who ordered it and you choose: a refund of everything you paid for that product within 14 days, or keep your order for the new ship date in that mail.
faq_q4: What if the ship date moves?
faq_a4: You get mail with the new date as soon as we know it. Until your order is delivered you can still cancel it for a refund.
faq_q5: Do I get one parcel or several?
faq_a5: One. An order ships once, complete, when every item in it is ready.
faq_q6: Do you ship to the United States?
faq_a6: Yes, for €19.95 per order. We do not collect US import duties at checkout: the carrier collects them from you before delivery. US import duty on electronics and motors made in China is high, often around 35 to 40% of the value. US customs sets the amount, not us, and the carrier can add a clearance fee.
faq_a7: No. A preorder pays for the production run of your own order. It carries no interest and gives you no equity, revenue share or other stake in the company.
faq_q8: Where do the numbers on this page come from?
faq_a8: From paid orders in our shop. Each product option counts only its own units, and the numbers refresh every minute.

faq_q_cancel: Can I cancel before it ships?
faq_a_cancel: Yes. Until your order is delivered you can withdraw from it without giving a reason: use the [withdrawal form](/herroepingsrecht#withdraw) or email contact@opendrone.be. We refund what you paid for it, including the standard shipping cost, within 14 days, to the payment method you used.
faq_q_duties: Do I pay import duties outside the EU?
faq_a_duties: Inside the EU there is nothing more to pay: prices include Belgian VAT. Outside the EU we do not collect import duties or taxes at checkout. Your country's customs may charge them, and the carrier collects them from you on delivery. For the United States that amount is high: US import duty on electronics and motors made in China is often around 35 to 40% of the value, and US customs sets the amount. Check your country's rules before you order, and see [Shipping](/shipping).
